page: OVHcloud c3-32-flex is a compute-optimized virtual instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs without multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2 GB RAM per core. The instance includes a bundled 50 GB local NVMe solid-state drive for local system and operational storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth limit of 2 Gbps. No graphics accelerators are present on this machine.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-quartile execution in single-core compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a strong stress-ng single-core score of 3077.28, a high PassMark memory score of 2972.08, and fast multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 209.36 GB/sec. Geekbench text processing and small-scale language model text generation also placed within the top 25 percent. The majority of sustained multi-core tests, such as Geekbench compilation, Ray Tracing, and PassMark CPU ratings, settled within median industry thresholds, reflecting consistent performance across steady compute workloads.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the non-hyperthreaded physical core architecture provides reliable per-thread execution consistency, preventing performance degradation caused by noisy neighbors on shared threads. The compact 50 GB local NVMe disk and 2 Gbps network pipe represent practical operational tradeoffs, favoring workloads that focus primarily on in-memory compute rather than massive persistent storage or extreme high-throughput distributed transfer. These characteristics render the instance suitable for distributed build jobs, CI/CD worker nodes, software compilation pipelines, and dedicated batch data processing.
description: OVHcloud c3-32-flex is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor at 2.3 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, it incorporates 32 GB of system RAM, a bundled 50 GB local NVMe SSD, and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs included. Benchmark measurements show top-quartile single-core CPU throughput, high memory evaluation scores, and strong text decompression rates, while overall multi-threaded processing maintains solid mid-tier output. The dedicated core configuration avoids hyperthreading contention, delivering predictable execution for compute tasks. Due to its balanced compute ratio and modest storage envelope, the instance is well suited for continuous integration runners, compilation pipelines, batch processing, and dedicated backend services.
